text:
support_lead: FYI — ACME opened an escalation: embeddings endpoint throughput collapsed after last deploy. Previously ~11k vectors/sec, now ~2k vectors/sec. Started 2026-03-12 10:12 UTC. Customer impact: timeouts and billing disputes. Request id sample: req_0a1b2c3d. Model: open-embed-12B, dimension=1536.

devon_ml: On it. Can you paste the exact request payload and observed vectors/sec? Any SDK changes or config flags from the customer?

support_lead: Here's the curl we received from the customer (redacted):
```bash
curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"open-embed-12B","input":["long text 1...","long text 2...", /* ~256 items */],"max_batch_size":256}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```
They reported vectors/sec ~= 2k. Before deploy they reported ~11k for similar payloads.

ashley_engineer: We traced customer requests in our queue logs — they were hitting max_batch_size=256 which wasn't previously common. Our batching aggregator allowed huge coalescing. Queue depth spiked: embeddings_queue.depth = 1187 at 10:13 UTC. When depth > ~500 we see latency amplification.

sanjay_infra: GPU telemetry (10:12-10:18 UTC window) on pool "dedicated-embed-a100":
```
GPU_util%: 92-97
SM_stall_cycles_high: true
Memory_alloc_pct: 42
Kernel_retries: 0
NVLINK_rx_drop: low
```
But interestingly GPU cycles are saturated while per-request throughput dropped. That usually means lots of small jobs or inefficiencies from batching/kernels. Also saw a worker restart at 10:15 (killed by oom-adj?).

alex_oncall: Could this be tokens/sec vs vectors/sec confusion? If inputs got longer token-wise, tokens/sec could be high but vectors/sec low. But customer payloads are similar lengths. Worth measuring avg_tokens_per_input.

devon_ml: I ran a local repro with similar batch sizes. Observed avg_latency_per_batch jumped from ~40ms to ~250ms when queue depth goes above ~500. Vectors/sec = batch_size / latency. For batch_size=256 and latency=250ms -> 1024 vec/s, which matches observed orders. The root cause looks like queue-induced coalescing causing extremely large batches that stress KV cache and attention kernels, increasing per-batch latency superlinearly.

ml-sre-bot: [Alert] embeddings_throughput_drop detected for pool dedicated-embed-a100 (start=1809004330). Severity: high.

ashley_engineer: Two immediate mitigations I'm proposing: 1) soft cap per-client max_batch_size to 64 at the ingress level; 2) throttle aggregator's max_coalesce_window from 100ms -> 50ms so batches don't grow too large. Both are low-risk.

sanjay_infra: I'm going to scale up the worker count by +20% on that pool to help drain backlog, and suppress autoscaler until we confirm shape. Pushing a drain job now.

devon_ml: Also noticed in the deploy we flipped default kernel profile to "quant-8-opt" for smaller models; for open-embed-12B that path increases sequence handling overhead. We should pin this model to fp16 kernels until we validate quant path for long sequences.

support_lead: Customer asked for repro steps — I'll share these:
1) Use their payload with batch_size=256.
2) Send at steady QPS ~60 req/s for 2 minutes to build queue.
3) Observe embeddings_queue.depth and p99 latency.

devon_ml: Repro command I used locally: 
```bash
python load_test.py --model open-embed-12B --batch 256 --qps 60 --duration 120 --endpoint https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings --auth $TOKEN
```
Output (sample):
```
requests_sent: 7200
avg_latency_ms: 212
p95_latency_ms: 410
vectors_per_sec: ~980
```
Matches customer.

ashley_engineer: Config change to cap batch size in our SDK (patch):
```json
{"embeddings": {"max_batch_size": 64, "batching": {"max_coalesce_window_ms": 50}}}
```
We'll rollout to ingress for all customers as a hotfix and provide an override for enterprise customers who explicitly opt in.

sanjay_infra: Hotfix deployed to ingress in canary at 10:35 UTC. Canary draining looks good — queue depth down to ~120. Will promote in 10 min if stable.

ml-sre-bot: [Info] canary rollout success for embedding-ingress-hotfix v2026.03.12-canary (id canary-778).

alex_oncall: For long-term: augment aggregator to be workload-aware: prefer more medium-sized batches to avoid superlinear latency. Also add per-model batching heuristics (longer sequences -> smaller batches).

devon_ml: I'll follow up with a perf test matrix of batch_size vs seq_len vs kernel_profile and publish recommended defaults. For now action items:
- ashley_engineer: enforce per-client cap + ingress hotfix (in progress).
- sanjay_infra: scale adjustments and monitor (in progress).
- devon_ml: perf matrix and pin kernel profile for open-embed-12B (ETA 24h).
- support_lead: communicate mitigation & repro steps to ACME and offer temporary SLA credit if they want.

support_lead: ACME accepted our mitigation and temporarily set client SDK override to max_batch_size=32. They've seen vectors/sec climb to ~9k and no timeouts. Closing escalation after post-mortem.

ashley_engineer: We'll schedule a runbook entry for "embeddings: queue depth induced batch collapse" and add golden signals (queue depth alarms) to prevent reoccurrence.

devon_ml: +1. Will include kernel_profile guardrails in model onboarding checklist.

support_lead: Thanks everyone. I'll keep thread open for the post-mortem doc and follow-ups.
